bash -c '
_re_allow_exclude="^\./(\$|\*|\.\$|\.\.(\$|/)|\.git(\$|/)|\.ssh(\$|/)|\.aws(\$|/)|\.kube(\$|/)|\.gnupg(\$|/)|\.docker(\$|/)|\.config(\$|/)|\.claude(\$|/)|\.env)"
_re_allow_list="^(\./[^/*.][^*]*|\./\.[A-Za-z0-9_-][^*]*|node_modules\$|node_modules/|dist\$|dist/|build\$|build/|target\$|target/|\.next\$|\.next/|/tmp/.+|out\$|out/|coverage\$|coverage/)"
for p in "./.Git/" "./.GIT" "./.CLAUDE/" "./.SSH/" "./.env" "./.git-old" "./.loa/" ; do
  ex="no"; al="no"
  [[ "$p" =~ $_re_allow_exclude ]] && ex="yes"
  [[ "$p" =~ $_re_allow_list ]] && al="yes"
  echo "$p  exclude=$ex allow=$al"
done
'

result:
I've completed the audit and written it to `audit.md`. Summary:

**Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED** (1 critical, 1 medium)

1. **Critical** — The new named exclusion list in `block-destructive-bash.sh` (lines 856-857) that replaced the old blanket "block every hidden path" rule is case-sensitive, while the new hidden-dir allow branch accepts any case. On case-insensitive filesystems (macOS default, Windows), `rm -rf ./.Git/`, `./.Claude/`, `./.SSH/`, `./.Env`, etc. bypass the guard entirely and delete the real `.git`, `.claude` (System Zone), `.ssh`, or `.env` directories — exactly what this hook exists to prevent. The old regex's blanket `\.` catch-all didn't have this gap; it's a regression introduced by this PR.

2. **Medium** — `find_local_source()` in `constructs-lib.sh` dropped the slug-matching validation (`_local_source_matches_slug`) entirely, so it now returns the first directory in the search list with a manifest file, regardless of whether it's the requested construct pack. When `local_source_paths` in config lists multiple local dev sources, this can silently substitute the wrong pack under the requested slug's identity.

One observation noted as sound hardening: the `symlink-manifest.sh` traversal-check simplification is equivalent-or-stronger than what it replaced (it now also checks the target string, not just the link).
